Lessons.Title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Reasoning
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: use the structure of squares and products to reason about all real solutions, including two roots, one repeated root or none, before formal algorithmic steps. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 3 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/3/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/3/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source accepts verbal reasoning and asks students to explain why squaring hides signs.

Original equation (x−3)²=16 implies x−3 can be+4 or−4; thus x7 or−1. Compare x²=0 with only root0, and x²=−9 with no real roots because the square of a real number cannot be negative. Even if a calculator produces no real square root, the conceptual reason matters.

An alternate quadratic equation 2x²=50 gives x²=25 and x=±5. The ± is required when taking square roots of a positive value. Do not confuse the principal square root √25=5 with the two solutions of x²=25.

Student task: solve at least one equation from each 0/1/2-real-root category by reasoning, show actual substitutions and explain a wrong solution that keeps only the positive branch. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for correct possibilities, both-square-root logic, verification and full explanation.

V13 source task detail: U7L3 asks students to reason about equations with zero, one or two distinct real roots, including products and shifted squares, then find BOTH roots of several shifted equations. The prior sample discussion emphasized shifted squares but insufficiently practiced factoring as a separate reasoning path or the one-root/zero-root boundary cases.

V13 original equation sort: (x+2)^2=25 has x=3 or x=-7; 3x^2=75 has x=5 or x=-5; (x-2)^2=0 has only x=2; (x-2)^2=-1 has no real roots; x(x-6)=0 has x=0 or6. Check each proposed root in the ORIGINAL equation, and identify which has no real root using nonnegativity of real squares.

V13 teacher note: the principal radical sqrt(25) denotes positive5, but an equation y^2=25 has BOTH y=5 and y=-5. Teach by reasoning about squares, not a mechanical claim that square-rooting is one-to-one. Optional extension may use degree-three factorizations; never present three or ten distinct real roots as possible for a nonzero quadratic.
